prompt:
Implement the token bucket rate limiter in src/rate-limiter.mjs. The file has a stub of the class RateLimiter (named export, ES module, no dependencies, Node only). Write the real implementation so it meets all of the numbered requirements below. test/basic.test.mjs has two simple tests; more tests that check each numbered requirement will be run.

API: `new RateLimiter({ capacity, refillPerSecond, now, idleTtlMs })` and the methods tryConsume(key, cost = 1), waitTimeMs(key, cost = 1), peek(key), reset(key), resetAll() and size(). Times are in milliseconds.

1. Constructor options. capacity must be an integer of at least 1, refillPerSecond a finite number above 0, now (optional, default Date.now) a function returning the current time in milliseconds, idleTtlMs (optional) a finite number above 0. Anything else throws a RangeError whose message is exactly `invalid option: <name>`, for example `invalid option: capacity`. A missing options object is the same as an empty one and so fails on capacity.
2. Every key has its own bucket. A bucket is created the first time tryConsume is called for its key and starts full, with `capacity` tokens. tryConsume returns a new object `{ allowed, remaining, retryAfterMs }`. When the tokens are enough, cost is taken, allowed is true and retryAfterMs is 0. When they are not enough, nothing is taken, allowed is false and retryAfterMs says how long to wait. remaining is the number of whole tokens left after the call (the token count rounded down), in both cases.
3. Refill is continuous: a bucket gains refillPerSecond tokens for every 1000 ms that pass, and fractions of a token are kept between calls, including between calls that were denied. A bucket that is asked every 250 ms at 2 tokens per second must allow a call every second call, not never.
4. A bucket never holds more than `capacity` tokens, however long it sat idle.
5. retryAfterMs is the time until the bucket holds `cost` tokens, in whole milliseconds rounded up. Calling tryConsume again exactly that many milliseconds later (with no other call in between) must be allowed. Example: capacity 4, 3 tokens per second, bucket empty, cost 1: 334.
6. waitTimeMs(key, cost) returns the same number retryAfterMs would be right now, or 0 when the tokens are already enough or the key has no bucket. It changes nothing: it does not create a bucket, does not take tokens, and does not count as use for requirement 9. It throws like tryConsume for a bad cost or key. peek(key) returns the whole tokens the key has right now (capacity for an unknown or expired key) and also changes nothing.
7. cost must be an integer from 1 up to capacity, otherwise tryConsume and waitTimeMs throw a RangeError with the message `invalid cost`. key must be a string (the empty string is allowed), otherwise tryConsume, waitTimeMs, peek and reset throw a TypeError with the message `key must be a string`. A call that throws creates no bucket.
8. reset(key) gives that key a full bucket again, resetAll() does so for all keys, and size() returns the number of keys that currently have a bucket (0 after resetAll). reset of a key that was never used does nothing.
9. When idleTtlMs is set, a bucket that has had no tryConsume call for idleTtlMs milliseconds or more is dropped, and the key then behaves like a new key, so it starts full even if its tokens had not refilled yet. Exactly idleTtlMs of idle time counts as expired, one millisecond less does not. A tryConsume call that is denied counts as use. size() does not count expired buckets. Without idleTtlMs buckets never expire.
10. If now() returns a smaller time than at the previous call that touched a bucket, no tokens are added for that call, and the bucket counts time from the new, smaller time from then on.
11. If now is not given, Date.now is used.
12. Return values are plain objects that the caller may change without affecting the limiter.

Run `npm test` for the basic tests, and write your own tests for the rest.
